title: N. Mock pages
description: The pages and the micro-frontends of the product's mock-up: a static frontend under `mock/`, one HTML page per screen on JSON fixtures and no backend. A micro-frontend is a Micro-UI as the mock shows it — a fragment on a fixture — injected in pages; what the factory view shows on its easel, and what the gates check every screen has.

title.description: What a human calls it in the list of pages.

objective.description: The user goal the page serves — the sentence the page was created from.

screen.description: The frozen screen composition this page mocks (`apps/screens/<screen>.json`), once it exists.

components.description:
The micro-frontends the page injects, by name: each is `
` in the page, filled by `mock/mock.js` from `components/.html`.
The micro-frontends the mock-up knows: one per Micro-UI shown, built or still to build.

description.description: What it shows and lets the user do — what the composer reads.

fragment.description: Its markup and script, relative to `mock/`: `components/RiskBadge.html`.

fixture.description: What its Capabilities would answer, as the fragment reads it.

actions.description: The DataCapabilities a user action may trigger.

source.description: The Micro-UI's folder this micro-frontend is built from (`apps/<system>/<micro-ui>`): the bundle is the real code on the mock server. Absent for a hand-written fragment.

builtFrom.description: Written by `mock/build.mjs`: a digest (FNV-1a 64) of the entry, the shared files under `mock/src/` and every file under `<source>/src/`, so the gates know the bundle is stale.

variantOf.description: The micro-frontend this one was forked from by a page's draft in the factory view: a copy the page edited, shown there instead of the origin. Build it as a variant of its origin, not a second Micro-UI.
